title: PM-Eng 1:1 runtime & routing / KV-cache coordination (Ana)
content:
Purpose / quick context:
- Prep for 1:1 with Eng Lead (Lina) — focus on short-term operational fixes and medium-term rollout decisions for routing + KV-cache updates that affect hosted API, Dedicated customers, and Private onboarding.
- Want clear decisions + owners for (A) routing policy changes to improve latency for small-chat workloads, (B) KV-cache consistency fixes that cause rare token duplication on fallback, (C) dedicated pool sizing guidance for Q2 pilot.

Top-line metrics to have on-hand (bring dashboard links in call):
- Hosted API: 95th pctl gen latency last 7d = 312ms (down from 330ms after batching tweak)
- KV-cache hit rate (hosted): 18% overall, but 42% for high-throughput chat routes (disparity = key)
- Dedicated pool utilization (pilot customers): avg 78% peak 94% (single region eu-west1)
- Private onboarding queue: 3 active customers in staging, avg time to first successful run = 6.5 days (blocked by KMS integration 2/3)
- Cost: estimate per-1M-token cost (hosted) drift +6% month-on-month due to retry volume spikes on version rollout 2026-02.

Agenda (30 min):
1) Last meeting quick sync (2m) — what I did on follow-ups, what you did
2) Routing policy experiment (8m) — can we temporarily prioritize low-latency routes for small-chats? tradeoffs?
3) KV-cache duplication/fallback bug (8m) — triage status, short-term mitigation, timeline for root cause fix
4) Dedicated capacity guidance for Q2 pilot (6m) — do we increase reserve, autoscale tweak, or introduce burst buckets?
5) Quick wins & action items (6m) — owners, deadlines, dependencies

Notes / talking points (more granular):
- Routing / policy
  - Problem: some small-chat customers are seeing tail latency > 450ms due to being routed to general-purpose nodes with large batching windows.
  - Hypothesis: adding a micro-route ("small-chat-low-latency") that pins to smaller-batch GPU workers with tighter batching window will reduce P95 by ~30–40% but increase per-token cost for those requests.
  - Questions for Lina: how sticky are routing rules for existing customers (risk of sudden cost impact)? can we do a canary with 10% of traffic for 48h and rollback if cost > threshold?
  - Ask: if we implement micro-route, I want a metric guardrail: P95 down, cost-per-request increase < 20% for the canary cohort, and no error-rate increase. Who owns the canary run? (SRE or runtime team?)

- KV-cache duplication / fallback
  - Symptom: rare cases where fallback to a compatible model variant leads to duplicate tokens emitted (observed in 7 incidents last 30d). Potentially a mismatch between prefix cache invalidation and new model's kv-serialization.
  - Short-term mitigation we can deploy: reverse the last auto-compatibility fallback for affected models and force strict model-variant mapping for rollouts until root cause fixed. This reduces availability for low-tier requests but avoids customer-visible duplication.
  - Risk: strict mapping will increase error rates for capacity spikes. Tradeoff to discuss with PM on customer SLAs.
  - Ask Lina: estimate for root cause dev fix (low/med/high effort) and whether we can ship a safer compatibility shim in 1 sprint. Also need a test harness for reproducing KV mismatch — do we have one? (If not, create small reproducer: model A->model B with same tokenizer but different kv-map).

- Dedicated pool sizing (Q2 pilot)
  - Pilot expectation: 3 customers, combined steady qps ~2200 rps, spiky peaks up to 4800 rps. Current reserved capacity (2x) leads to 78% avg utilization but little headroom for burst.
  - Options:
    * Increase reserve to cover 99th percentile — cost increase but predictable latency
    * Keep current reserve, enable burst capacity using shared spare pools with auto-fallback if reserved exhausted
    * Add throttle-based admission control at API layer for non-SLA routes (complex but lowest cost)
  - Quick ask: Lina's recommendation? I lean to 2 + burst pool (hybrid) for pilot; want feasibility and estimate of engineering effort (infra and console changes) by EOD Thurs.

Decisions needed (explicit):
- Approve canary of micro-route for small-chats (10% traffic, 48h) with cost guardrail of +20% per-request limit. Decision: yes/no.
- Force strict model-variant mapping for the next 2 weeks for affected models or accept sporadic duplication for higher availability. Decision: strict-mapping/accept-risk.
- Dedicated pilot capacity approach: hybrid reserve + burst or increase reserve. Decision: which to pursue for the pilot.

Open questions to surface:
- Is there an automated billing alert we can wire to the canary to detect cost-per-token regressions? (I know we have infra metrics but not tied to cost yet.)
- Do we have an automated regression test for kv-cache behavior across model-variant fallbacks? If not, who will own the small reproducer and where to put it?
- For Private deployments: are customers comfortable with strict mapping during onboarding windows? Might affect time-to-value. Need to confirm with Solutions Eng (Ethan) before broader policy.

Action items (capture during meeting; pre-fill suggestions):
- Lina: confirm who runs the canary and give SRE contact (ETA: today) — owner: Lina; due: 2026-03-11
- Ana (me): draft canary runbook + metric guardrails and share with Lina/SRE — owner: Ana Rivera; due: 2026-03-12
- Lina + runtime eng: estimate effort for KV-cache compatibility shim and test harness — owner: Lina & runtime eng; due: 2026-03-18
- Ana + Ethan: sync with Solutions Eng on Private onboarding policy impact — owner: Ana Rivera, Ethan Brooks; due: 2026-03-13
- Infra: propose Dedicated pilot config (hybrid reserve+burst) with cost model for Q2 pilot — owner: infra-ops (TBD); due: 2026-03-14
- Ana: update pilot one-pager with chosen capacity approach and publish to Confluence — owner: Ana Rivera; due: 2026-03-15

Notes-to-self / stash (things I might say):
- "We can accept a small delta in cost for a measurable P95 improvement, but we need visibility and a kill-switch."
- "If KV duplication is user-visible (customers complain), we lose trust faster than small cost increases. Prioritize correctness over cost for this issue"
- "Canary should run in staging-like topology but with real traffic mirror if possible. Avoid synthetic-only testing — behavior only shows up under real request shapes."

Parking lot / future items (don't block call):
- Long-term: policy-driven routing UI in Console (let customers opt-in to low-latency micro-route) — product idea for H2.
- Investigate smarter caching heuristics (LRU vs LFU + request type signals) and tie to Optimize recommendations.
- Better cost telemetry per-route (product ask) — add to roadmap if small engineering lift.

Communication snippets (post-meeting):
- Short message to SRE: "We plan to run a 48h canary for a small-chat low-latency route (10% traffic). Need a run owner and guardrails attached. Please coordinate rollback automation. See Confluence CONFLUENCE-RT-2048 for details."

Last minute checks before the call:
- Dashboard links loaded and show last 60m window
- Canary runbook skeleton in PR open (link in chat)
- Quick note to Solutions Eng about potential Private onboarding impact (cc Ethan)

End of doc — quick free-form:
- Jot: if Lina suggests delaying strict mapping due to customer SLA concerns, suggest a middle ground: strict mapping except for customers with explicit opt-in to fallback. Write up template email to customers for this scenario.
- Reminder: capture meeting decisions in Jira tickets; set watchers = Product, Runtime, SRE, Solutions Eng.
